title: Pietro Sala
text:
Pietro Sala is an applied economist working on agricultural, water and resource economics. He is a PhD candidate (expected April 2027) and research associate at the Chair of Agricultural Production and Resource Economics, TUM School of Management, Technical University of Munich.
His research measures how efficiently farms and food systems use natural resources, and how to separate weather-driven losses from managerial shortfalls. Methodologically he works with stochastic frontier analysis, productivity and eco-efficiency measurement, panel econometrics and causal machine learning (double/debiased ML, LASSO). He has worked on two EU research projects: PONDERFUL (ponds as nature-based solutions) and RETOUCH NEXUS (water governance and the water–energy–food–ecosystems nexus), and coordinates the chair’s research partnerships in Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia).

title: About Mithril Metrics
text: Mithril Metrics publishes short, reproducible case studies on agri-food, water, climate and rural policy. Each one starts from a current policy debate, asks one narrow empirical question, and answers it with public data in about four hours.

title: About Mithril Metrics
text:
How each case is built

Public data only. Every number traces to a named dataset and access date.
One question, one answer. The bottom line comes first; caveats are stated plainly.
Methods from production and resource economics: production frontiers, productivity and efficiency measurement, water economics and governance, risk and fat tails, panel and causal-ML econometrics.
Reproducible. All code is on GitHub and runs end to end in R.
Neutral. Policy implications are written as trade-offs, not recommendations.

title: About Mithril Metrics
text:
Use of AI tools
We use Claude, an AI assistant by Anthropic, as a working tool: to help with coding, data retrieval scripts and first drafts of text. Questions, methods, robustness checks and conclusions are our own, every number is reproducible from the published code, and we review all text before it goes online.

title: Juan Pablo Henao
text:
Juan Pablo Henao is an applied environmental economist working on water economics and water governance. He is a doctoral candidate and research associate at the Chair of Agricultural Production and Resource Economics, Technical University of Munich.
His research covers water pricing and cost recovery under the EU Water Framework Directive, environmentally sustainable productivity growth in EU agriculture, and the efficiency of irrigation water management. He combines optimisation, stochastic frontier analysis, data envelopment analysis and econometrics in R. In the Horizon Europe project RETOUCH NEXUS he leads the work on water governance indicators, building on the OECD Principles on Water Governance.
Before TUM he worked for three years at FAO in Rome, designing environment and climate projects for Global Environment Facility funding in Latin America and the Caribbean and in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Earlier, at CEDE, Universidad de los Andes, he valued ecosystem services and coastal nature-based solutions and studied artisanal fisheries in marine protected areas. He holds an M.Sc. in Applied Economics and a B.Sc. in Mathematics from Universidad de los Andes.
